description.value: This study investigated gray matter volume alterations and causal structural covariance network relationships in recent-onset typhoon-related PTSD using structural MRI.

spans.text: This study aimed to explore the progressive profiles of the structural network throughout the symptoms of the illness and to further evaluate the causal effect of structural changes in patients with PTSD using CaSCN analysis.

value: normalization to Montreal Neurologic Institute space

spans.text: First, all images were checked for the presence of artifacts and reoriented to adjust image origins at the anterior commissure. Second, T1-weighted images were normalized to Montreal Neurologic Institute space; segmented into GM, white matter, and cerebrospinal areas; and resampled to an isotropic image resolution of 2 × 2 × 2 mm 3 . After the image quality and sample homogeneity were checked, the segmented GM images were smoothed with an 8-mm full width at half maximum Gaussian kernel. Finally, the GM optimal threshold mask, created with images of all subjects, was applied to eliminate non-GM voxels
smoothed with an 8-mm full width at half maximum Gaussian kernel

description.value: High-resolution T1-weighted anatomical images were artifact-checked and reoriented, normalized to Montreal Neurologic Institute space, segmented into gray matter, white matter, and cerebrospinal fluid, resampled to 2 × 2 × 2 mm isotropic resolution, smoothed with an 8-mm FWHM Gaussian kernel, and masked using a group gray-matter threshold mask. CAT12 in SPM12 was used to generate gray-matter volume images for group comparisons and CaSCN analyses.
